paper.title: An efficient algorithm to compute the genus of discrete surfaces and applications to turbulent flows (Algorithm 964)
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 42(4), 2016, article 34 (DOI 10.1145/2845076); read copy: arXiv:1709.00822

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 964.zip (fetched 2026-11-27), sha256 eb7b9a946d9b87a49972ed1740a0a38d9669ae281efd645240abe1c7c5cec496. Fortran 90 serial version at Fortran90/Src/fortran_serial (mainMod.f90, genusMod.f90, Makefile) and the shipped dataset Fortran90/data/random.128.dat; the documentation (Doc/documentation.tex, section Example) says the results should match case Random2 in Table III.

field: numerics (computational topology of voxel surfaces; turbulent-flow applications)

claim.location: Table III ('Summary of some of the datasets tested'), row Random2: size 1283, faces 2744830, edges 5489660, vertices 2570182, genus 87325. The genus column is the claim. The text (Section 5) says Table III lists the cases available for download; the archive's documentation names Random2 as the case that random.128.dat reproduces.

reference.file: arXiv:1709.00822 PDF, Table III (read copy, text extracted with pdftotext -layout)
reference.note: The published TOMS version may differ from the arXiv version; the rerun must record which one it compared against.

claim.metric: Genus of the discrete surface built from the voxel array in random.128.dat (128 x 128 x 128 cubical grid), as printed by the shipped genus program for the Random2 row of Table III.

tolerance.basis: The genus is an integer count from the Euler characteristic of an exact voxel surface, so any difference is a real difference. Fixed before any run. The rerun may not loosen it.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Estimated under a few minutes on one core (not measured). The paper's Figure 8 gives average serial times in seconds for cubical arrays on a Xeon X5650; the 128^3 case is well below the largest sizes shown.
cost.data_size: random.128.dat, 2097164 bytes, shipped in the archive.
cost.data_licence: Not stated in the archive; a Collected Algorithm from ACM. The rerun should record the licence it finds.

why: The paper prints the exact integer genus of the Random2 dataset in Table III, and the archive ships the dataset and the program that computes it, so a deterministic integer can be checked against a published table without any external download.
